diagnostics.reason: C003 is a mathematical source-identifiability check, not a premise for the requested classification. Its alternative-data witness records that the absent a-stack alone fixes neither a=N nor zero absolute production; MAIN instead uses the explicit dark-control model obligation.

C004 checks source-only non-identifiability of the LED assignment. The page-3 diagram contains Gibbs state differences, not activation barriers or optical thresholds, and no LED-indexed relation; the countermodel therefore remains separate from MAIN, which uses the explicit selectivity model obligation.

fields.meaning: H2 mole percentage for each chart category; the entry for a category without a stack is unconstrained and unused. This is composition, not absolute production.

fields.meaning: Photon energy indexed by condition code 0=N, 1=R, 2=G, 3=B. Only codes 1–3 denote LEDs; the value at N is unused.

lemmas.statement: Source axiom from the paragraph above the page-4 chart and item 8.8: the four distinct conditions N, R, G, B are to correspond one-to-one with a, b, c, d, so the unknown assignment is bijective.

lemmas.lean_type: experiment.stack_present 0 = false ∧ experiment.stack_present 1 = true ∧ experiment.stack_present 2 = true ∧ experiment.stack_present 3 = true
lemmas.statement: Source axiom from the central page-4 chart: a has no colored stack, while b, c, and d each have an H2/CO stack.
Source axiom from the blue-diagonal H2 portions and legend in the page-4 chart: the plotted H2 mole percentages have the strict order b > c > d.

For the three LEDs named above the page-4 chart, the Planck–Einstein law E=hc/λ and the visible wavelength order λB<λG<λR give EB>EG>ER. This finite color-energy comparison asserts no absorption or kinetic behavior.

lemmas.lean_type: ∀ i j : Fin 4, experiment.category_to_condition i ≠ 0 → experiment.category_to_condition j ≠ 0 → experiment.photon_energy (experiment.category_to_condition i) > experiment.photon_energy (experiment.category_to_condition j) → experiment.h2_mole_percent i > experiment.h2_mole_percent j
lemmas.statement: Pending finite LED-selectivity contest-model obligation: among the three irradiated conditions in this experiment, a higher photon energy implies a higher H2 mole percentage. It is not asserted as a universal photocatalysis law.

lemmas.lean_type: experiment.stack_present 0 = false ∧ ∃ alt : Experiment, alt.stack_present = experiment.stack_present ∧ alt.h2_mole_percent = experiment.h2_mole_percent ∧ alt.photon_energy = experiment.photon_energy ∧ Function.Bijective alt.category_to_condition ∧ alt.category_to_condition 0 ≠ 0 ∧ alt.total_product_amount 0 > 0
lemmas.statement: Source-identifiability diagnostic: while retaining the plotted stack flags, mole percentages, and photon energies, an alternative finite data model can assign a to a condition other than N and give a a positive unobserved absolute product amount. Thus absence of the a-stack alone establishes neither a=N nor zero formation.

lemmas.lean_type: ∃ alt : Experiment, alt.stack_present = experiment.stack_present ∧ alt.h2_mole_percent = experiment.h2_mole_percent ∧ alt.photon_energy = experiment.photon_energy ∧ alt.total_product_amount = experiment.total_product_amount ∧ Function.Bijective alt.category_to_condition ∧ alt.category_to_condition 0 = 0 ∧ ∃ i j : Fin 4, alt.category_to_condition i ≠ 0 ∧ alt.category_to_condition j ≠ 0 ∧ alt.photon_energy (alt.category_to_condition i) > alt.photon_energy (alt.category_to_condition j) ∧ ¬ (alt.h2_mole_percent i > alt.h2_mole_percent j)
lemmas.statement: Source-identifiability diagnostic: even with a=N and all recorded response and energy data fixed, there is a bijective R/G/B assignment violating energy–H2 monotonicity. The page-3 ΔG plot cannot exclude it: its labeled state differences are neither activation barriers nor optical thresholds, and it gives no LED-indexed relation.

lemmas.statement: C006 restates the same finite energy–H2 relation as C002. Its direct target follows from L006 and introduces no additional model assumption.
Because the assignment is bijective, N occurs at one category; L009 makes that category stackless, and L002 shows a is the unique stackless category. Hence a=N.
After a=N, bijectivity makes b, c, d a permutation of B, G, R. Their H2 order b>c>d, the photon-energy order B>G>R, and strict monotonicity force b=B, c=G, and d=R.

main_statement: The requested classification is a=N, b=B, c=G, and d=R.
